subject: Integration & Observability follow-up: SDK setup, auth, routing, embeddings, trace headers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Integration & Observability follow-up: SDK setup, auth, routing, embeddings, trace headers

Alex — I'm great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call so the engineering teams can move forward:

1) Goals (as we discussed)
- Integrate Redwood text generation/chat and embeddings for multi-step payments flow and transaction enrichment
- Add observability hooks to correlate model calls with your tracing and fraud signals

2) Priority integration areas for FintechCo
- SDK setup & auth: use server-side API key for backend calls; recommend mTLS for high-risk endpoints (Dedicated/Private).
- Routing: route low-latency requests to our us-west region; fall back to cheaper quantized variants for batch jobs.
- Structured output/tool calling: we'll return JSON schema (tool-calling) for downstream parsers — include schema version header.
- Embeddings & reranker: will create a small embedding index for transaction descriptions and use a reranker model for top-N.

3) Observability hooks (what engineering asked for) — attached I included a one-page header checklist: observability-headers.txt
- Trace ID: Redwood-Trace-Id (send your trace id in X-Request-Id and we echo it back)
- Latency breakdown headers we will return: X-Total-Latency / X-Queue-Time / X-Model-Latency / X-Cache-Hit
- Token counts returned in X-Tokens-Consumed (per request)
- Request-level metadata: route-id, model-version, quantization-profile (as headers)
- Example: X-Request-Id: 6b8f3c2a-...; Redwood-Trace-Id: rwd-20270612-9f4

4) Next steps (proposed timeline)
- Today: I'll upload the integration checklist + example headers (attached).
- Tue 6/15: Engineering sync (30m) — Dev (your infra) + Ethan (our runtime) to agree on auth and routing TTLs.
- Wed 6/16: Dev shares sample auth flow and IP allowlist needs.
- Goal: staging integration by end of month.

We'll also provide a small SDK snippet for quick verification (server call + echo headers) and a sandbox endpoint for testing. I attached the Redwood integration checklist and observability header examples.

If any of this is off, call it out and I'll update. Otherwise can we lock in Tue 6/15 11:00 PT for the engineering sync?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.pdf, observability-headers.txt

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration & Observability follow-up: SDK setup, auth, routing, embeddings, trace headers

Thanks Marissa — really useful summary. A few clarifications from our infra side:

- We prefer short-lived server-side keys with rotation; mTLS is possible but may take longer for procurement.
- For routing, can you confirm how the fallback to quantized variants impacts latency headers? Will X-Model-Latency reflect the quantized model run?
- For embeddings/reranker: can you provide expected embedding dimensionality and approximate cost per 1k items?

Also looping in Sarah (payments infra). Can Priya from your side join the engineering sync?

Yes to Tue 6/15 11:00 PT if that works for you and your engineers.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
alex.chen@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration & Observability follow-up: SDK setup, auth, routing, embeddings, trace headers

Alex — good questions. Quick answers and tech owners below; Dev and Ethan will add technical detail on the engineering sync.

- Short-lived keys: supported. We'll provide rotation guidance and sample server flow.
- Quantized fallback & latency: X-Model-Latency is the model execution time for the variant we used; X-Total-Latency = X-Queue-Time + X-Model-Latency + network. We'll add a header X-Model-Variant to indicate quantization profile (e.g., q4_0, int8).
- Embeddings: default config is 1536 dims for our production embedding model; we can provide a smaller 768-dim option for cost-sensitive workloads. I'll attach an estimated cost per 1k items in the PRD link.

Priya will join Tue 11:00 PT — thanks for asking. Dev/Ethan — can you prep the example header echo endpoint and a sample cURL + SDK snippet that returns the headers (X-Request-Id, Redwood-Trace-Id, X-Model-Latency, X-Total-Latency)?

Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration & Observability follow-up: SDK setup, auth, routing, embeddings, trace headers

Alex / team — quick technical notes ahead of Tuesday:

1) Example header behavior (we'll deploy a sandbox endpoint you can hit):
- You send: X-Request-Id: 6b8f3c2a-1234
- We return: X-Request-Id: 6b8f3c2a-1234; Redwood-Trace-Id: rwd-20270612-9f4; X-Model-Variant: q4_0; X-Cache-Hit: false; X-Queue-Time: 12ms; X-Model-Latency: 85ms; X-Total-Latency: 110ms

2) SDK snippet (server-side, Node example) — we'll paste into the sync doc but high level:
- Initialize SDK with server API key
- Call client.generate({ prompt, stream:false, headers: { 'X-Request-Id': uuid(), 'fintech-route': 'payments' }})
- Check returned headers and payload; if X-Cache-Hit=true we can short-circuit for certain flows

3) Auth modes we support: server API key (short-lived tokens), OAuth client-credentials for platform integrations, and per-customer mTLS for Dedicated/Private.

4) Embeddings sizing: we can provision a 1536-dim index; recommend sharding by customer-id for fast reranks. Cost estimate posted in PRD.

I attached the observability-headers.txt with header names and example values. Will be in the shared drive after the sync.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
